name: Physical Education
intro: Explore the decisions, relationships and evidence behind performance. Suggested BGE themes are examples, not a prescribed school programme. Practical participation follows teacher guidance, inclusion arrangements and school safety procedures. Independent work here involves analysis and reflection, not unsupervised training plans, fitness testing or exercise regimes.

bge.title: Team decisions
bge.question: What makes a team effective?
bge.task: Analyse a teacher-selected game clip and draw an alternative supporting position.
bge.extend: Explain how the best decision changes when opponents change their formation.

bge.title: Skills and feedback
bge.question: How can feedback improve learning?
bge.task: Use a supplied performance description to write one specific strength and a next learning step.
bge.extend: Explain why several small changes at once might make progress hard to evaluate.

bge.title: Performance factors
bge.question: Why does performance vary?
bge.task: Analyse a fictional performer’s situation using at least two different factors and supporting evidence.
bge.extend: Explain how factors can interact rather than operate independently.

bge.title: Inclusive participation
bge.question: How can sport welcome more people?
bge.task: Redesign the rules of a fictional school activity to improve participation while retaining its purpose.
bge.extend: Explain how to gather participant feedback without making assumptions about ability.

senior.title: Physical Education
senior.explain: Develop practical performance and understanding of factors affecting it. National 4 includes added-value performance.
senior.assessment: Internally assessed units and National 4 added value; pass/fail.

senior.title: National 5 Physical Education
areas: Physical, mental, emotional and social factors
senior.explain: Use evidence to understand performance and develop skills in teacher-selected activities.
senior.assessment: Performance and portfolio under current national requirements. Independent reflections are practice, not ready-made portfolio answers.

senior.title: Higher Physical Education
senior.explain: Connect data collection, approaches to development and evaluation with physical, mental, emotional and social factors.
senior.assessment: Performance and question paper. Teachers confirm activities, adaptations and current assessment requirements.

skills.title: Collect useful evidence
skills.explain: An observation method must match the factor being investigated.
skills.try: Design a paper checklist for decision-making in a teacher-selected clip.
skills.check: Does it record a specific observable behaviour consistently?

skills.title: Explain performance factors
skills.explain: Link a factor to an identifiable effect in context.
skills.try: Explain how concentration could influence a passing decision.
skills.check: Give a cause-and-effect chain rather than simply saying performance improves.

skills.title: Set process targets
skills.explain: Targets identify a controllable action and a way to review it.
skills.try: Write a target for communication during teacher-led practice.
skills.check: State what will be observed and when teacher feedback will be reviewed.

skills.title: Evaluate fairly
skills.explain: Use comparable evidence before judging an approach.
skills.try: Compare two fictional observation records with different opponents.
skills.check: Acknowledge contextual differences that limit the comparison.

practice.question: A player completes 18 of 24 passes. Calculate pass completion and identify a limitation of this measure.
practice.hint: Convert the fraction to a percentage; consider difficulty.
practice.answer: 18/24 × 100 = 75%. The percentage does not show pass difficulty, pressure, distance or tactical value. Combine it with relevant observations.
practice.extend: Explain why two players with 75% completion might contribute differently.

practice.question: A performer loses concentration after making an error. Explain a possible effect and a suitable discussion point for the teacher.
practice.hint: Connect attention to a specific next decision.
practice.answer: Attention may remain on the mistake, delaying recognition of an available pass or defensive responsibility. Discuss a teacher-approved refocusing cue and how its effect could be observed.
practice.extend: Distinguish concentration from a physical factor such as endurance.

practice.question: A team wins after changing its tactics. Does this prove the new tactics caused improvement?
practice.hint: Consider opposition and other contextual factors.
practice.answer: No. Opposition, player availability, conditions and chance may also matter. Use repeated comparable observations and process evidence, not the result alone, to evaluate the change.
practice.extend: Identify a measure that could show whether the tactical aim was achieved.

resources.title: sportscotland
resources.task: Explore coaching or inclusion resources and identify an example of supportive practice.

resources.title: Scottish Disability Sport
resources.task: Explore available sport resources and explain how an adaptation supports participation.

resources.title: Youth Sport Trust
resources.task: Investigate leadership or inclusive participation and propose a school discussion question.

resources.title: Olympic education
resources.task: Evaluate a sporting-values example using a specific action and its impact.

resources.title: Understanding Standards PE
resources.task: Discuss published examples and assessment expectations with your teacher; some evidence is staff-only.

ipad.title: Tactical analyst
steps: Pause at three decision points and annotate space or positioning.
Explain a possible choice and its consequence.
ipad.evidence: A reasoned analysis, with copyright and recording permission respected.

ipad.title: Feedback notebook
steps: Add brief evidence after a supervised lesson.
Review the target using one specific observation.
ipad.evidence: A personal learning reflection with no health or identity details shared publicly.

ipad.title: Inclusive design
steps: Create a diagram of a fictional activity space.
Annotate one rule, equipment or space adaptation.
Explain how you would seek participant feedback.
ipad.evidence: An inclusion proposal ready for teacher discussion, not a home exercise task.

careers.title: Sports coaching
careers.linkToLearning: Observation, communication and inclusive planning support participants.
careers.nextStep: Explore college sports coaching and governing-body qualifications.

careers.title: Physiotherapy
careers.linkToLearning: Anatomy and movement analysis connect to further healthcare study.
careers.nextStep: Check degree entry and professional registration requirements.

careers.title: Leisure and recreation work
careers.linkToLearning: Safety awareness and customer support help run facilities.
careers.nextStep: Investigate leisure apprenticeships and local college pathways.

careers.title: PE teaching or sports development
careers.linkToLearning: Analysis, leadership and inclusive practice support learning and participation.
careers.nextStep: Compare university teacher education and sports development routes.

parentTip: Ask about a decision, teamwork moment or learning target rather than only a score. Encourage participation and teacher-guided progress without comparing bodies or prescribing extra training.
